Along: from one part of a road, river, etc. to another.

"A romantic walk along the beach/river."

In: inside a container, place, or area, or surrounded or closed off by something.

"I got stuck in a traffic jam for half an hour."

Of: used to show possession, belonging, or origin.

"A friend of mine."

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Such problems include difficulty in implementing decisions, providing social security to everyone and ensuring employment.

B. This is because almost all countries face problems related to their population.

C. The most crucial aspect of the problem is population pressure.

D. The population explosion is an important issue these days.
questions.solution:
The correct order is DBAC.

Sentence B cannot be the beginning of the passage. Sentences A and C talk about a problem. Sentence D states that the problem discussed in the passage is the population explosion. Therefore, sentence D comes first. B follows D as it states why this issue is important. A follows B as it describes different problems which are faced by all the countries. C follows A as it states that the core of all this problem is population pressure.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Radha said, "why didn't he forward his petition to me?"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Radha said, "why didn't he forward his petition to me?"

options.text: Radha enquired why he had not forwarded his petition to her.
options.html: Radha enquired why he had not forwarded his petition to her.

options.text: Radha enquired why he has not forwarded his petition to her.
options.html: Radha enquired why he has not forwarded his petition to her.

options.text: Radha enquired why had he not forwarded his petition to her.
options.html: Radha enquired why had he not forwarded his petition to her.

options.text: Radha enquired why he had not forward his petition to her.
options.html: Radha enquired why he had not forward his petition to her.

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

For example:

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Past tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past perfect tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'enquired'.

· The verb ''didn't forward'' is changed into ''had not forwarded''.

· The pronoun 'me' is changed into 'her'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Radha enquired why he had not forwarded his petition to her.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Electrolytes like P. important for balancing the water in your body Q. are present in the body's fluids and are R. are electrically charged minerals that S. sodium, potassium, chloride and magnesium
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Electrolytes like

P. important for balancing the water in your body

Q. are present in the body's fluids and are

R. are electrically charged minerals that

S. sodium, potassium, chloride and magnesium
questions.solution:
The correct order is SRQP.

The beginning of the sentence is 'Electrolytes like'. Therefore, the phrase that follows should give examples of electrolytes. Phrase S comes first as it gives examples of electrolytes. Phrase P cannot follow as it is grammatically incorrect [because of absence of any verb]. So, option (b) is incorrect. The pair QR is also grammatically incorrect [because of redundancy - helping verb 'are' would be repeated]. So, option (c) is also incorrect. Option (d) gives a coherent sentence.

The sentence after rearrangement is: Electrolytes like sodium, potassium, chloride and magnesium are electrically charged minerals that are present in the body's fluids and are important for balancing the water in your body.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. The dog was terrified by the unexpected noise.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

The dog was terrified by the unexpected noise.

options.text: The unexpected noise had terrified the dog.
options.html: The unexpected noise had terrified the dog.

options.text: The unexpected noise terrified the dog.
options.html: The unexpected noise terrified the dog.

options.text: The unexpected noise has terrified the dog.
options.html: The unexpected noise has terrified the dog.

options.text: The unexpected noise terrifies the dog.
options.html: The unexpected noise terrifies the dog.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['was' in the given sentence] and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): The unexpected noise terrified the dog.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

She likes you. (Active Voice)

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. He always / aimed highly / in life.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

He always / aimed highly / in life.
questions.solution:
In the givens sentence, the adverb 'highly' is used to qualify the verb 'aimed'. The sentence conveys that the subject aimed for high achievements. Generally speaking, the adverbial form of 'high' is 'high'. The adverb 'highly' is used as an intensifier. It is usually used to qualify another adjective or adverb. Therefore, in the given sentence 'highly' should be replaced with 'high' to rectify the given sentence.

So, the error is in the part in option (c). Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: He always aimed high in life.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 1.
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Tediously: in a boring way that continues for a long time.

Industrially: in a way that relates to industry.

The blank requires an adverb to qualify the adjective 'recognised'. The sentence talks about the tea industry. The previous sentence highlights the position of the Indian industry in the world. Therefore, 'globally' is the most appropriate adverb that can replace the blank.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 2.
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Complex: not easy to analyse or understand; complicated or intricate.

Establish: set up on a firm or permanent basis.

Pampered: indulge with every attention, comfort, and kindness; spoil.

Equipped: having sufficient equipment, supplies.

The blank requires a noun to describe the tea industry. Option (b) is a verb. It is eliminated as it cannot act as an adjective. The past participle verb 'equipped' or 'pampered' can act as an adjective. After observing the meanings of the given options, we can say that 'equipped' is the most appropriate choice that can replace the blank.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The blank requires a noun as it follows the preposition 'for' which requires a noun after it.

Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Fulfilment: the achievement of something desired, promised, or predicted.

Advantage: a condition or circumstance that puts one in a favourable or superior position.

Consumption: the action of eating or drinking something.

Retention: the continued use, existence, or possession of something or someone.

The sentence conveys the uses of tea. We all know that tea is one of the common beverages in India. Therefore, the word 'consumption' is the most appropriate choice here.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.
